REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT A. Francisco Gold Condominium II EDSA Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG Opinion No. 16 s. 2011 ØIVAHENG PINOY HON. RENATO S. MUNEZ, M.D. Vice-Mayor Municipality of La Paz Province of Agusan del Sur MAY 09 2011 THRU: Legislative Staff Officer Mr. Lito S. Munez Dear Vice-Mayor Munez: This has reference to your request for opinion on whether or not the previous year's budget on intelligence funds may be re-enacted despite the violation of DILG Memorandum Circular No. 99-65 (hereinafter referred to as "M.C. No. 99-65"), i.e., no funds are allocated for peace and order concerns, and with reference to the opinion of COA Chairman Reynaldo A. Villar concurred to by then BLGS Director, now ASEC Rolando M. Acosta in his 29 August 2008 letter to former, which quoted a portion thereof in your letter. 1 In reply to your letter, please note that Item II, paragraph no. 2 of M.C. No. 99-65 explicitly provides the following: "2. Funds for Intelligence or Confidential purposes may be sourced from the: (a) appropriations for peace and order; or (b) total annual appropriations. X X X" (Emphasis ours) Clearly, M.C. No. 99-65 does not confine the sourcing of funds for intelligence or confidential purposes to appropriations for peace and order but also from the total annual appropriations in the alternative. As regards the letter of ASEC Acosta to COA Chairman Villar which you cited as basis, we have noted based on the official copy of said letter from our Records Section that the entire views and/or opinion concurred to by ASEC Acosta are the following, to wit: "1. That if an LGU considers peace and order as a priority program, it must allocate funds for peace and order from out of its annual budget; 2. if no funds are allocated for peace and order concerns, it is understood that there is no need to utilize funds for intelligence purposes; and 3. that to determine the amount to be utilized for intelligence and confidential purposes, it shall be based on the: (a) 30% of the peace and order allocation, or 3% of the annual appropriations, whichever i lower, " (Emphasis ours) 1 "1. If no funds are allocated for peace and order concerns, it is understood that there is no need to utilize funds for intelligence purposes. 2. That to determine the amount to be utilized for intelligence and confidential purposes, it Shal/ be based on (a) 30% Of the peace and order allocations, or (b) 3% of the annual appropriation whichever is lower. "

It is apparent that paragraph no. 2 should be taken within the context of paragraph no. I. This is in accord with the provision of M.C. No. 99-65 on the source of funds for intelligence and confidential purposes. Keeping in mind the above discussion, we now come to the issue on whether the previous year's budget may be re-enacted for failure of the sanggunian to override the veto of the local chief executive notwithstanding that a violation of M.C. No. 99- 65 was committed. Before we discuss the same, may we direct your attention to Art. 415 (b), 2nd paragraph, 2nd sentence of the Implementing Rules and Regulations of Republic Act No. 7160 which provides as follows: "(b) x x x The vetoed items shall not take effect unless the sanggunian overrides the veto in the manner provided in Rule XVII of these Rules; otherwise, the item or items in the appropriations ordinance of the previous year corresponding to those vetoed, if any, shall be deemed reenacted." The IRR of R.A. No. 7160 provides for the automatic re-enactment of the previous year's budget for failure of the sanggunian to override the same. The re-enactment of budget is not affected by any perceived infirmity of the previous year's budget because it is presumed valid as approved by the sanggunian. Furthermore, the LGUs operations, projects and activities will be hampered without the necessary funds based on the re-enacted budget of the previous year. This does not mean however that violations by any local official as regards intelligence and confidential funds may be committed with impunity. Any erring local official shall be subject to sanctions under the Local Government Code and other applicable laws on the matter. We hope to hav enlightened you on the matter. Very truly yours, . JE Director III LS08:rb B. OQUE IV Opinion La Paz Agusan DS
